description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 1 + CHECK 2).  PRE-EXISTING.
The CAUSE of `comp/parser.t`'s 93-row shortfall and of 72 of its 140 blessed
fail rows (the `ok -> (missing)` half).

The blessed `sig` for the file names **#1276**, which is an ATTRIBUTION-DEBT
task about the COUNT snapshot being stale -- it says nothing about why the
rows fail.  This task is the row-level cause.

THE FIVE DROPS, as the compiler announces them (#339), from this tree's
transpile of t/comp/parser.t:

  line 432  "${; =pod =cut }";
            Bug. Fell through. Missing case:
              ['Statement::Null<;>','Token::Pod<=pod ...]
  line 456  sub 'Hello'_he_said (_);
            Bug. Fell through. Missing case:
              ['Token::Quote::Single<'Hello'>', funcall]
  line 733  <<EOW;
            Bug. Fell through. Missing case:
              ['Statement<check_line(537,...)>','Statement::Null<;>',
               'Statement<check_line(538,...)>']
  line 733  <<EOX;          (the same shape, the second heredoc on the line)
  line 764  <<"END";
            Handle single node of unknown type.

They are five of the SIX drops the whole `comp/` directory produces (the sixth
is comp/final_line_num.t's, which is deliberately invalid perl), and they are
in `baselines/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv` -- so the census already counts
them; what was missing is that they are also 72 test ROWS.

WHY 72 AND NOT 5: the drops sit in the middle of the file's `#line`-tracking
section, whose rows are `check_line(N, 'desc')` calls INSIDE interpolated
heredoc bodies.  A dropped `<<EOW;` statement takes its heredoc's
interpolation -- and therefore the `check_line` calls in it -- with it, and the
recovery load then abandons the rest of that top-level form.  The blessed rows
that go missing are the whole `after here-doc in quotes` / `first|second line
of interp in here-doc` / `line number after ...` family plus the tail.

WHAT THE OTHER 68 FAIL ROWS ARE (classified by reading the source line each
description belongs to, `scratch/s473t5c/classify-parser.pl`):
  44 assert `$@`'s text for INVALID perl (VCS conflict markers, `Bad name
     after foo::`, `syntax error in string with incomplete \N`, over-long
     identifiers) -> not-supported.md §Error compatibility for invalid Perl
     input + §Error message text;
  24 are a genuine SCATTER (#1695) -- `"${a}{"` interpolation, stash effects
     after a compilation error, `__PACKAGE__` is read-only, heredocs inside a
     string eval, `format` inside a re-eval.  1.04 rows per distinct
     assertion: this file is `op/`-shaped, not `comp/`-shaped.

FIX ORDER, if it is taken: the three `<<HEREDOC;` drops are one shape and the
biggest prize (the whole `check_line` family); the `=pod` inside `"${…}"` and
the quoted sub NAME are one-offs and are both INVALID-ish perl that perl
nonetheless parses.  All five are Option B phase 2 material
(`docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md`), not `$end_pars`-region edits.
subject: t/comp/parser.t's 72 never-produced rows: FIVE #138 drops (a `=pod` inside `"${…}"`, a quoted sub NAME, three bare `<<HEREDOC;` statements) plus the abort they leave behind
